skills.name: Talking about pandemics and contagious diseases; reading about an outbreak

note.text:
A contagious disease passes from one person to another, for example cholera, measles, tuberculosis and COVID-19. An epidemic is when many people in one area catch a disease at the same time; a pandemic is an epidemic that spreads across many countries, like COVID-19 in 2020.
In the text, cholera spread through dirty water and food. The sick lost water through diarrhoea and vomiting. They were treated with oral rehydration salts (ORS) and in hospital. Families boiled their water, washed their hands with soap and used latrines.
Malaria is a serious illness, but it is not contagious: mosquitoes carry it from person to person, so we sleep under a mosquito net.
Talking about illness: “What are the symptoms?” “How does it spread?” “How can we prevent it?”

worked_example.problem: Answer three questions about {d} from the text: How does it spread? What are the symptoms? How can we prevent it?
steps: How it spreads: people drink dirty water or eat food that is not clean.
Symptoms: watery diarrhoea and vomiting, so the body loses water.
Prevention: boil or treat drinking water, wash hands with soap, use latrines.
worked_example.answer: It spreads through dirty water and food; it causes diarrhoea and vomiting; we prevent it with clean water, handwashing and latrines.

cards.idea: Read the text about a cholera outbreak.
example: Last rainy season there was an outbreak of cholera in a town near the coast. Cholera is a contagious disease: it spreads when people drink dirty water or eat food that is not clean.
The sick had watery diarrhoea and vomited, so their bodies lost a lot of water. Nurses gave them oral rehydration salts (ORS) mixed with clean water, and the very sick were treated in the hospital.
Health workers went from house to house. They told families to boil or treat their drinking water, to wash their hands with soap and to use latrines. After a few weeks, the outbreak ended.

cards.idea: Contagious means it can pass from one person to another. An epidemic spreads in one area; a pandemic spreads across many countries.
example: Malaria is not contagious: mosquitoes carry it.

cards.idea: To talk about an illness, ask about the symptoms, how it spreads, and how to prevent or treat it.
example: What are the symptoms? — A high fever and a cough.
How can we prevent it? — Wash your hands with soap.

questions.prompt: One sentence is NOT true. Which one?

right.text: Washing hands with soap removes germs.
ORS helps a body that has lost water.
A pandemic spreads across many countries.

wrong.text: Malaria passes from person to person when they shake hands.
wrong.explain: Malaria is carried by mosquitoes; it is not contagious.

wrong.text: An epidemic is a medicine against cholera.
wrong.explain: An epidemic is many people catching a disease at the same time.

wrong.text: Cholera is treated with mosquito nets.
wrong.explain: Nets prevent malaria; cholera is treated with ORS and hospital care.
